units.text: Dana wins the game through a choice she cannot defend very well. This time, she has the generosity to admit it. It does not spoil her pleasure. Her friends collect the pieces, and the world need not know who truly deserved that cardboard continent.

Andrei closes two additional projects and leaves only one on next week’s list. In his log, he notes that the agent saved implementation time and that part of the gain was consumed by verification. He has no slogan about the profession’s future. He has a somewhat better process for the next task.

Mara changes her title. For now, the word “theory” becomes “hypothesis.” The imagined experiment does not confirm the idea’s most ambitious form, but brings to light a distinction she had not noticed. It is not the end of research. It is the first day when research can answer differently from what she hoped.

These endings are fictional and deliberately open. They do not promise that a log, a test, or a stopping rule solves every problem. Some users need professional support, some organizations need shifts in power, and some questions require years of research.

Yet something has changed. The three no longer use the same word for different experiences. Dana was lucky and had fun. Andrei built something verifiable. Mara learned something that can change her idea.

The machine at the beginning could pay in possibilities, meaning, and confidence. The workshop at the end asks some of these to become things that hold up outside the conversation. Not to drive out wonder, but to give it a world to work with.

Sometimes the most intelligent continuation is not another answer. It is a test. At other times, a question asked of a person. And sometimes it is simply closing the window without feeling that you have just missed the meaning of the universe.
